method: 5 read-only lenses; P0-P2 adversarially verified (default refute); P3 kept unverified

lenses.summary:
Lens: assisted-order admin session isolation (6d64d3e fix, 7a35394 tests), checked at c0e25c7. Between 6d64d3e and c0e25c7 only the test file was added under client/src/research/assisted-order and pages/adminx, so the runtime under review is exactly 6d64d3e. I found no P0, P1 or P2 defect.

1. Request A response rendering into request B: prevented.
   - AdminAssistedOrderDetail.tsx:28 remounts the detail per requestId.
   - The per-instance `mounted` ref (:41-49) makes every continuation from an unmounted instance a no-op.
   - The GET and the PATCH both check that the server echoes the same requestId (:66, :98-101).
   - Each instance closes over its own requestId, so a PATCH or document ticket can never target another request.
   - Covered by the tests at test.tsx:433-452.

2. Cross-actor and sign-out bleed: prevented, apart from one tiny window (F2).
   - AdminAssistedOrderSession.tsx:21-23 bumps a generation whenever the token or session state changes, and :57 keys the child tree on it.
   - isCurrent (:29-31) requires: same generation, state "ready", a non-null token, and not denied.
   - A 401/403 latches denial for all outstanding work (:32-38).
   - The queue gates its debounce timer and promise on both `alive` and isCurrent (Queue.tsx:34, 42, 45, 49).

3. Double-submit:
   - Within one mounted detail, the `updating` ref is set before the first await (:76-77) and the button is disabled while busy (:181).
   - Across remounts the client does not guard. The server does: the RPC is a compare-and-set on the expected status (supabase-repository.ts:483-485), and no status may transition to itself (service.ts:85-109). A duplicate gets a 409, not a second transition or customer notice.

4. Implied success:
   - The client never shows a status change as succeeded unless the server returned 2xx with a matching requestId.
   - A 204 or null body throws into the error path.
   - 409, 401/403 and network errors show an error or the denied screen.
   - When a response is lost, the client either shows an error or drops the response silently (F1). It never shows success.

5. Authority: the client only withholds data and actions.
   - Every call still sends the bearer token to requireSupabaseAdmin routes (server/index.ts:1129-1132).
   - The server grants every admin all three capabilities (express.ts:38-42), so latching denial on any 403 is not too broad today.
   - Paid stays server-refused (service.ts evidenceRequired).

The 26-case count in docs/health-launch/ADMIN_ASSISTED_SESSION_ISOLATION_20261001.md matches the test file. Its claim at line 61 is slightly too strong; see F2.

p3.claim: A routine token refresh for the same admin is handled as if the session changed. The page remounts, silently drops an in-flight status PATCH result (success or refusal), and wipes the draft and queue filters. A dropped refusal looks almost the same as a success.
p3.evidence: Supabase is created with autoRefreshToken: true (client/src/lib/supabaseBrowser.ts:105). On TOKEN_REFRESHED, useAdminSession calls setToken with the new access token (pages/adminx/auth.ts:77-80). AdminAssistedOrderSession.tsx:21-23 bumps the generation on any token change, and :57 remounts the children through Fragment key={generation}. In the old detail instance, the PATCH result is dropped at AdminAssistedOrderDetail.tsx:97 (`if (!current()) return;`) and any refusal is dropped at :51 (`failed` returns early). So a 409 such as financial_resolution_required or payment_verification_not_ready never reaches the screen. The new instance starts with empty fields and nextStatus 'reviewing' (:35-38), and its GET runs at the same time as the old PATCH, so it can show the status from before the PATCH. A successful update also clears the fields (:103-105) and shows no explicit success message, so a refused update can look like a completed one; only the 'Current status' heading tells them apart. Queue search, status and page also reset (Queue.tsx:19-21). The test at AdminAssistedOrderSession.test.tsx:298-328 accepts this, using a token swap as a stand-in for a different actor. No test separates a same-user refresh from an actor change. Server compare-and-set (supabase-repository.ts:483-485) and the ban on self-transitions (service.ts:85-109) keep a retry from duplicating a transition. Fix: key the generation on actor identity rather than the raw access token, or re-read the request and show an 'outcome unknown, re-check status' notice when an in-flight PATCH is dropped.
p3.reachability: Reachable now wherever the assisted-order admin routes are composed (client route adminx-section.tsx:163-164; server doors index.ts:1129-1132). It happens about once an hour per open admin tab when the access token auto-refreshes, and also when a hidden tab's expired token refreshes on return. Dropping the PATCH result needs the refresh to land during the PATCH round trip, which is rare. Wiping the draft and filters happens on every refresh. No data crosses actors and no server authority is affected.

p3.claim: isCurrent() checks the last rendered auth state, not the latest auth event. A document ticket that resolves after the sign-out event but before React re-renders can still call window.open.
p3.evidence: scope.current is updated only during the session component's render (:21-23), and isCurrent reads it (:29-31). Supabase's SIGNED_OUT callback calls setToken(null) and setState('signed_out') (auth.ts:77-80). That schedules a normal-priority render, which runs in a later task. Until then, isCurrent() still returns true for the old generation, so a ticket that resolves in that gap passes the check at AdminAssistedOrderDetail.tsx:118 and runs window.open at :119. Other state updates landing in the same gap are harmless, because the re-render remounts the tree. Only the window.open side effect escapes. Doc line 61 says document links open 'only after a successful result still belongs to the current mounted session/request', which is slightly too strong. Fix: mirror the auth state into a ref inside the auth callback (or check a session-epoch ref updated by the auth listener) before window.open.
p3.reachability: Reachable now but very narrow: a single scheduler tick between the auth callback and the re-render. It needs the same admin to have clicked 'Open securely' before signing out (in this tab or another), with the ticket arriving in that tick. It cannot carry data from one admin to another, because signing in as someone else takes far longer than one render.

lenses.summary:
HL01 lens review at runtime c0e25c7. The lens files are byte-identical to ed5c5ad/928dfc6, and the records tip is 8549011. Overall the slice is sound, with one minor copy defect on held rows (P3).

1. **No price in the disclosure.** The <details> block (AssistedOrderPage.tsx:200-221) has no price field in any of the five workflow modes. Care rows get only Specification, Format, Pack basis and a provider-review notice: no Research quantities, and the server also nulls Care price and priceVersion (action-policy.ts:156,163).
2. **Inspection is separate from ordering.** The disclosure is an uncontrolled native details/summary. It has no onToggle or click handler, no React open-state, and no a/button/input inside it. No ancestor click handler or form wraps the card, and Add, the Care CTA and quantity controls all stay outside the disclosure (lines 226-302). Opening or closing it cannot select, persist, navigate or submit.
3. **Accessibility is acceptable.** Native disclosure semantics (no redundant role or aria-expanded). The accessible name starts with the visible label "Product details" and adds product and specification through the existing .xenios-order-sr-only class (css:16). The summary has a 44px minimum height and a 3px accent focus-visible outline.
4. **Long-fact wrapping works.** min-width:0 plus overflow-wrap:anywhere on the card and the details (css:53,65) lets the flex and grid min-content shrink without clipping. In the real member-safe dataset the longest unbroken label token is 38 characters ("AOD-9604/MOTS-C/TESAMORELIN/IPAMORELIN") and it has slash and hyphen break opportunities, so no real-data overflow is expected. The selection summary (line 967) and review lines (line 1050) were not given the same wrapping. They would only matter for synthetic unbroken strings, and the docs honestly limit browser evidence to an empty request.
5. **Docs are consistent with the code.** The records-tip packet (docs/health-launch/HL01_CATALOG_DETAILS_20261001.md:14-16) does not overclaim.
6. **Pre-existing, outside the disclosure, not reported as a finding.** The card face renders money(unitPriceCents) for availability_review rows (line 198). The server only nulls price for provider_request, so a bound and priced held row would show a dollar amount next to "Temporarily Unavailable". This is currently latent: the only customer-visible held rows are GRP-0422 (binding_pending) and GRP-0365 (quote_only), and both are unbound, so they show "Price on request". The new test at AssistedOrderPage.test.tsx:445 asserts "$25.00" on a held fixture card. That conflicts with the Early Access lane's held-no-price rationale (earlyAccessCatalogView.ts:102-105), but the cross-lane policy is ambiguous (customer-pathway.ts:16 accepts "priced and held").

The single finding is below.

p3.claim: The disclosure only special-cases Care (careOnly). Held / temporarily-unavailable rows (availability_review) therefore fall into the Research branch (lines 211-219). That branch shows "Minimum request quantity", "Maximum request quantity", "Quantity increment" and "Request quantities only, not dosing instructions. Availability is confirmed separately." It does this for rows the same card says "cannot be added to an order request right now" (lines 246-253). The disclosure presents request terms and a pending-availability promise for rows that cannot be ordered. The text is not a control, so no ordering authority leaks.
p3.evidence:
Line 209: `{careOnly ? (

Care options and quantities require separate provider review.

) : (<>...Minimum request quantity...Maximum request quantity...Quantity increment...

Request quantities only, not dosing instructions. Availability is confirmed separately.

)}`. The availability_review rows are not excluded (`unavailable` is computed at line 175 but not used in the disclosure). In production, authorityFor sets maximumQuantity to EARLY_ACCESS_POLICY_MAX_QUANTITY = 100 for every row (server/research/assisted-order/production-catalog.ts:200; shared/research/early-access-quantity.ts:47). Two customer-visible held rows today: GRP-0422 'CJC-1295 WITH DAC + IPAMORELIN 5 mg total' (formulation hold, binding_pending) and GRP-0365 'Syringes & Alcohol Swabs' (shipping_and_fulfillment, so non_merchandise_family, so held; quote_only). Neither is excluded by service.ts:71-75, which drops only GRP-0364. Both would show 'Maximum request quantity 100' plus 'Availability is confirmed separately'. Tests lock this in: AssistedOrderPage.test.tsx:446 (it.each including heldItem) and :842 ('Maximum request quantity': '7' on a held row). By contrast the Care branch deliberately withholds Research quantities (docs/health-launch/HL01_CATALOG_DETAILS_20261001.md:16). Fix: treat availability_review like Care in the disclosure: drop the request-quantity facts and use held-specific copy.
p3.reachability: Reachable now on the mounted /research/early-access/order-request route and the embedded Early Access order page, for the two production held rows. It is copy and presentation only: no add, submit, price or money path is reachable through it, because selectableInResearchRequest and server submit-refusal still block held rows.

lenses.summary:
The Codex claim checks out: the form is not mounted on the current public journey. At c0e25c7, research/section.tsx renders PartnershipInquiryForm through four routes: :307 supplier-access, :340 organizations, :341 partners (PartnerPathwaysPage, via pages/partners/Landing) and :342 affiliates. App.tsx:246-249 redirects those exact four paths to /partners, /practices and /suppliers before the `/research/*` route at :259. Both routers use the same default wouter 3.10 parser (exact match, optional trailing slash, case-insensitive), and there is no custom Router, base or nest. Any URL the section would match is therefore redirected by App first. Section aliases (/research/wholesale, /professionals, /access) all lead to /research/partners and then to /partners. The clarity pages use their own InquiryForm. No other importer mounts the form.

Form review at c9677cb (unchanged through c0e25c7):
- **Receipt binding is correct.** The heading, the follow-up email line, the "Submitted email" and "Relationship type" rows, the summary textarea and the clipboard text all come from the `submitted` snapshot (:192) or receiptRef (:223/:233), never from the live draft. `name` and `summary` are read from the same render closure.
- **Duplicate-submit guard holds.** The synchronous ref guard (:128) is set before the first await (:188), and the button is disabled while submitting.
- **Unmount guard holds.** The cleanup nulls the refs, isCurrent() blocks late setState, and stale clipboard results are dropped by the generation counter (:225-227).
- **Copy is honest.** Success depends on server success:true, which /api/contact returns only after Resend accepts the team email (contact-delivery.ts:30, email.ts:217; a missing provider throws). The confirmation line follows the real autoReplySent flag. No copy claims inbox delivery or an established partnership; the intro and footer say the opposite. The form does not send `website`, so the honeypot path cannot fake success. The idempotency payload is deterministic.
- **Tests.** c9677cb did not change the test file. The regression tests landed later in test-only commit aeae38e (records tip). They cover a delayed receipt after edits, the clipboard snapshot, a retry after an uncertain failure, a duplicate submit in one render, late resolve/reject after unmount, a stale clipboard result and Strict Mode.

One latent P3 (PIR-01), detailed in the finding above: after an uncertain failure where the user edited the form mid-flight, the error copy wrongly says the details are still in the form and that a retry is duplicate-safe. No P0, P1 or P2.

p3.claim: If the user edits the form while a submission is in flight and that submission then fails as uncertain, the error copy says the details are still in the form and that retrying is duplicate-safe. Neither is true then: the attempted snapshot has been thrown away and the form holds different, edited values. A retry sends a different payload, gets a different idempotency key, and can produce a second team email.
p3.evidence: At c0e25c7: inputs are not disabled while submitting. update() (:110-115) is not gated on `submitting`, and it clears submitError. On failure, the catch at :210-213 calls clearReceipt() and sets submitError, and the `submitted` snapshot built at :192 is dropped. Line 432 then renders `{submitError} Your details remain in this form. Receipt has not been confirmed.` submitError carries the uncertain text from client/src/lib/waitlist-service.ts:39 or server/routes.ts:462: "Your message may already have been accepted. Keep the same details and retry shortly; unchanged retries within 24 hours are protected against duplicate email." Deduplication only works for byte-identical payloads, because the key is a sha256 of {from,to,replyTo,subject,text} (server/services/email.ts:215). The records-tip test "retains a later draft after an uncertain result and binds an explicit retry to its own payload" (added in aeae38e) asserts this flow: edit during flight, rejection, retry with the new email. So the behaviour is intended, but the copy in that state still promises protection the retry does not have. Impact: at most one extra team-inbox email. No money, data or safety exposure.
p3.reachability: Latent. The form is not mounted on the current public journey. I confirmed this at c0e25c7. Only research/section.tsx renders the form, through four routes: :307 /research/supplier-access (SupplierPartnershipPage), :340 /research/organizations (OrganizationAccessPage), :341 /research/partners (PartnerPathwaysPage) and :342 /research/affiliates (AffiliateAccessPage). App.tsx:246-249 redirects those exact four paths to /partners, /practices and /suppliers before the catch-all `/research/*` at App.tsx:259. Both routers use the same default wouter 3 regexparam parser (`^...\/?$`, case-insensitive), with no custom Router, base or nest anywhere. So any URL that would match a section route matches the earlier App redirect first. Section's /research/wholesale, /professionals and /access redirect to /research/partners, which App then sends to /partners. pages/Wholesale.tsx is imported only by a test. The clarity pages use clarity/InquiryForm.tsx instead. Becomes reachable only if a legacy B2B route is remounted.

lenses.summary:
I checked the records lens against runtime c0e25c7 and records tip 8549011. Every check (a) to (f) holds. I found no P0, P1 or P2 overclaims, only two small P3 wording problems.

(a) Migration 94 has exactly nine `create or replace` functions:
- Six consumers with a narrowed hold check: uncertainty, create_context, settlement_guard, financial_eligibility, settlement_row_allowed and financial_guard. Each now holds only orders that reserved the affected source; before, one unbound event anywhere held every order.
- attempt_guard, which gains the check that refuses a first reservation into an already-quarantined source.
- settlement_integrity (the seal regex changes) and schema_fingerprint.

It also adds two private helpers and one partial index. I diffed every body against its effective predecessor in 91-93: the only change is the hold predicate, and no other global unbound-event check is left in SQL or server TypeScript. Sources really are unique on (provider_namespace, account_ref, mode) (migration 91, line 101).

(b) The canonical LF blob sha256 of 3b0f13d7 is 91a20f681038a5e845137feb6556c4041b1645f6b2c8f9122bc7c9e85280f477. That matches the handoff, MIGRATIONS.md, MIGRATION_DAG.json and run2's migrationSha256. The file is unchanged from c0e25c7 to HEAD.

(c) The DAG node lists only research_assisted_order_quote_provider_settlement (row 93, 20261001115512) as its dependency. It is sourceSha c0e25c7, appliedToProduction false, managedMigrationId PENDING, and the DAG has 53 nodes. The release-control-plane.test.ts pending-source map pins the file to c0e25c7.

(d) The archive's canonical blob hash is 2540281f… and all 16 log hashes check out. The full-suite log reads 2 failed / 1020 passed / 6 skipped files (1028) and 3 failed / 19443 passed / 85 skipped tests, 1425.26s, log hash 4a86e028. That equals the handoff, PROJECT_STATE, RELEASE_STATE and BLOCKED_EXTERNAL. These archive numbers also match the handoff:
- the three failures (static.ts hash, three seam hashes, pgcrypto timeout at 13,749ms);
- the affected-tests run (1368 passed, 1 skipped, 43 files);
- run2 (14 groups, 27 refusals, 8 races, 150.637s);
- the DAG and route checks;
- the 37-of-38 protected hashes passing;
- the 24 process samples, one with a null path (PID 37108).

The committed test harness bytes equal the hashes run2 recorded.

(e) Nothing changed between 8f24082 and HEAD in CORE_SITE_PROTECTION_MANIFEST.json, any manifest file or seam path, scripts/, core-site-protection.test.ts or pgcrypto-qualification.test.ts.

(f) None of the records claims managed or production application. All of them carry claudeAccepted=false and managedQualified=false. F1, GATE-01, G2-G4, REFUND-ABSENT and LENS-01 adoption are all stated as open, matching Claude report24 at 7660745. The LENS-01 handoff's archive hash 119547ca (106,523 bytes) checks out, and that slice changed no migration bytes.

Remaining problems are two P3 wording issues.

p3.claim: The execution index says adpg1-install-smoke applied the exact migration twice locally, but nothing ties that run to the committed bytes of migration 94. The same overclaim appears in the identical blob at .xenios/handoffs/2026-10-01T18-31-05-247Z-HEALTH-HL12-ADPG1-QUARANTINE-ISOLATION-...md:117.
p3.evidence: adpg1-install-smoke-start.json records head aba12d6, and dirtyAtStart shows the migration as untracked ('?? supabase/migrations/20261001160730_..._quarantine_isolation.sql'). The run ended at 16:13:39.855Z. Commit c0e25c7, which first committed the file, is dated 2026-10-01T11:16:07-05:00 (16:16:07Z), about 2.5 minutes later. The migration actually replaces nine functions, and eight bodies change: settlement_integrity is also rewritten (seal regex ADP03 to ADP04Q). lenses.summary:
Read-only review of c0e25c7 (migration 20261001160730) against predecessors 085559, 102904, 115512, 040351, 044200 and 062651. I found no unscoped "established_request_id is null" check left in any effective function body. The successor replaces all six global consumers: uncertainty, create_context, settlement_guard, financial_eligibility, settlement_row_allowed and financial_guard. Every place that still mentions it is in a superseded predecessor body. No migration later than 160730 exists at c0e25c7.

Paths checked and found to hold, each with a scoped check:
- **Requests with a provider attempt:** assert_clear always holds them (provider_attempt_held). That covers manual observations and verifications, observation corrections and their replacement rows, quote issue/accept and reissue, no-funds context/evidence/disposition (via the wrapped disposition_graph), and cancellation.
- **Settlement:** settlement admission and the paid transition use request_quarantine_held under the request lock, then the fence, in READ COMMITTED.
- **Post-settlement transitions:** these go through eligibility, which checks quarantine first.
- **Provider rows:** provider-method rows are admitted only through settlement_row_allowed, which is quarantine-scoped.
- **Replays:** settlement replay and create_claim replay return receipts and write nothing.
- **Late results:** create_result_append on an existing claim only retains the response and binding; settlement stays gated.
- **Retrieve under quarantine:** a 'retrieve' claim is still allowed, as it was before the successor. It does not move money.
- **Payment-effects outbox:** payment_effects_complete (040351:266-297, with the provider allowance at 115512:437-449) can release a held "Payment verified" email after the source becomes quarantined. It changes no money or fulfillment state, repeats a paid event the order timeline already shows, and was also unchecked under the old global predicate. Not reported as a G1 escape.
- **Read-only server readers:** financial_state and the status/member-history readers do not authorize anything; the database triggers do.
- **Manual-only orders:** I found no new over-hold. A reservation on a quarantined source is refused before it is inserted, so it cannot strand an order.

One new, latent escape is reported below. The successor assumes a journal row's source_id is the event's real provider account and mode. The TypeScript ingress breaks that assumption on purpose: an authenticated event that names a different account or mode is filed under the configured source, with all claims stripped.

verified.claim: The new source and request quarantine checks key on journal.source_id. But the ingress files any authenticated event that names a different provider, account or mode under the configured ingress source, with all claims stripped. The source the event actually belongs to (another configured source, e.g. the live one) is therefore no longer held. The old global predicate held it, and the ingress code's own comment still promises a 'global uncertainty hold'.
verified.evidence:
Ingress, server/research/assisted-order/payment/provider-journal.ts:
- Line 173 computes validScope against this.source.scope.
- Lines 175-177: 'Invalid scope strips all binding claims and becomes a global uncertainty hold', then claims = validScope ? event : {}.
- Line 195 always appends with p_source_id: this.source.sourceId and p_expected_scope: this.source.scope.
- provider-journal.test.ts:184-191 confirms that {mode:'live'}, {accountId:'other-account'} and {provider:'other'} mismatches are stored under the test source 'synthetic-source' as kind 'unknown' / unknown_attempt.

SQL side:
- The journal guard (085559:439-440) checks only the configured expected_scope, so the row lands with source_id = the ingress source.
- 160730:41-43 (source_quarantine_held) and 160730:51-54 (request_quarantine_held: join attempts a to journal j on j.source_id=a.source_id) only hold attempts on that ingress source.

These replace the global predicate (115512:287 eligibility, 115512:350 paid transition, 115512:199 settlement admission) in 160730:280, 160730:332, 160730:238 and the 160730:91 reservation refusal.

Failure scenario: sources S_test and S_live are both configured (the unique (namespace, account, mode) key allows this). Order R_live has settled through S_live (status paid, with a bound captured event). Later, an authenticated refunded or dispute_opened event for R_live's payment, declaring mode 'live', reaches only the S_test ingress. The adapter accepts it, the claims are stripped, and the journal gets an unbound row with source_id=S_test. Then:
- request_quarantine_held(R_live) is false, and R_live's settlement graph is unchanged.
- financial_eligibility returns fulfillmentEligible=true.
- financial_guard (160730:335-338) allows paid -> supplier_processing -> shipped.
- source_quarantine_held(S_live) is false, so new live reservations are also admitted (160730:91).

Before c0e25c7, 115512:287/350 held R_live. In reverse, test-mode events delivered to a live endpoint permanently quarantine S_live for events that, by their own authenticated content, are not S_live's.
verified.reachability: Latent (default-off/unmounted). buildAssistedProviderJournal, buildAssistedProviderExecution and buildAssistedProviderSettlement are not composed anywhere in non-test server code. No sources, policies or grants are seeded, and migration 94 is pending and local-source only. It becomes reachable once ingress is activated with two or more configured sources (test plus live, or multiple accounts) and an authenticated cross-scope event arrives at the wrong ingress. Must fix before provider ingress or settlement is activated. Possible fixes: SQL keeps a non-source-scoped (global) hold for scope-mismatched events (TS would need to mark them, e.g. retain the declared scope or a scope_mismatch reason), or the ingress refuses such events instead of filing them under its own source.

verdict.reasoning:
Confirmed at c0e25c7 as a latent P2. One detail of the reachability claim is wrong, and the precondition is narrower than the finding states.

How the code behaves:
- server/research/assisted-order/payment/provider-journal.ts:173 compares the event's provider, accountId and mode against this.source.scope.
- Lines 175-177 say an invalid scope "becomes a global uncertainty hold", then set claims = {}.
- The fact sent to SQL has a fixed set of 16 keys (085559:335-337) and none of them carries scope. Line 195 always appends with this.source.sourceId and this.source.scope.
- The journal guard (085559:438-440) only checks the configured expected_scope. Classification (085559:395) gives reason unknown_attempt with established_request_id null.
- So the row is filed under the receiving source only. provider-journal.test.ts:184-191 confirms that provider, account and mode mismatches all get this stripped, unbound treatment.

What c0e25c7 changes:
- It replaces every global `exists(... established_request_id is null)` check: 115512:199 (settlement), :287 (eligibility), :309 (canonical-row admission), :350 (paid transition), plus the uncertainty check at 085559:225.
- The replacements are source_quarantine_held (160730:39-44, keyed on j.source_id) and request_quarantine_held (160730:49-55, join on j.source_id = a.source_id). They are used at 160730:70, 91, 169, 238, 280, 301 and 332.
- settlement_graph (115512:103) only includes rows with established_request_id = the request. An unbound row under a different source therefore changes neither R_live's graph nor its quarantine state.
- Result: eligibility (160730:280-288) returns fulfillmentEligible = true, and financial_guard (160730:335-338) allows paid -> supplier_processing -> shipped. Before c0e25c7, 115512:287 and :350 held R_live.
- The TS comment at provider-journal.ts:176 now makes a promise the SQL no longer keeps.
- Multiple sources are allowed: 085559:101 only makes (namespace, account, mode) unique.
- Nothing in 160730 (including lines 380-424) adds any global component back.

Corrections and limits:
1. Reachability is misstated. The three builders *are* composed in non-test code, at server/index.ts:1050-1072. They are passed source: null, so sourceValid fails and each returns null. Migration 94 is pending (MIGRATIONS.md:783). The finding's conclusion still holds: this is latent and needs a code change to activate.
2. The precondition is narrow. provider-adapter.ts:72 requires adapter authentication to check account and mode. A conforming adapter at S_test would reject a live event as unauthenticated, and R_live would then not be held either. So the regression only shows up when an adapter returns ok for an event from another scope. The ingress handles exactly that case on purpose and promises a global fail-closed hold for it, which c0e25c7 drops.

Other notes:
- The reverse direction (test events reaching the live endpoint quarantine S_live) is only a liveness concern. It is narrower than the old global freeze, so it is not a regression.
- A fix needs TS and SQL together, because stripped rows look the same in SQL as ordinary unknown_attempt rows. Two options: keep a global, or declared-scope, hold for rows marked as a scope mismatch; or have the ingress refuse scope-mismatched events.
- This must be resolved before provider ingress or settlement is activated with more than one configured source.
